transcript:
Header: QBR - Ursa Ventures Health Check 
Date/Time: 2025-10-08 15:00 PT | Duration: ~42 min
Attendees: Emma Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Karen Holt (Ursa), Samir Patel (Ursa CTO), Lina Alvarez (Ursa)

Summary: quick quarterly review of usage/cost trends, a couple reliability blips in Sept, discussion about moving from hosted to dedicated for low tail latency, and next-step actions on security docs and a pilot.

Topics: usage, costs, reliability incidents, Dedicated vs Hosted, security/SOC2, pilot next steps

[00:00] Emma (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we'll run about 40 minutes, quick agenda: usage, costs, reliability, then roadmap and next steps.
[01:00] Karen (Ursa): Thanks, Emma. Quick note — Samir has to drop at 40, so if we can keep the pilot conversation before then that'd be great.
[02:00] Samir (Ursa): Yep, real tight window today. Also, we saw a cost spike in September from embeddings, want to understand root cause.
[03:00] Diego (Redwood): Got it. We've pulled the token-level breakdown — prelim shows a change in batch sizes and some retry storms from a downstream job. We'll include that in the report.
[04:00] Karen (Ursa): There were some backfills in our pipeline, we didn't throttle them properly, so yeah that could be it. Also curious about KV cache settings you mentioned in the doc.
[05:00] Emma (Redwood): Right, KV/prefix caching can cut token costs for repeat prompts — Diego will go over suggestions in a sec.
[06:00] Diego (Redwood): For your workload profile (short instructive prompts + repeated context) enabling prefix caching and bumping the batch timeout to 20ms improved throughput in our tests without hurting latency.
[07:00] Lina (Ursa): What about quantization and model variants? We are using a 13B open model — can you quantify latency gains vs quality?
[08:00] Diego (Redwood): Quantization (4-bit) reduced GPU memory and allowed higher concurrency; we saw 15-25% latency improvement on p99 for long sequences, with minimal quality regression on your evals. We can run a short eval on your staging prompts.
[09:00] Karen (Ursa): That would be helpful. Also security — compliance team asked for SOC 2 and details on KMS/HSM integration.
[10:00] Emma (Redwood): We'll share our SOC 2 report and the KMS integration whitepaper today. For Private/VPC, we can surface HSM options via our enterprise channel.
[11:00] Samir (Ursa): On reliability, we had two incidents mid-September: about 5–7 minutes of elevated error in one region and a fallback to smaller model. Can you explain the fallback?
[12:00] Diego (Redwood): The fallback was automated policy — when we detect GPU unavailability for the pinned model we route to a compatible variant to keep requests alive. We log and surface those events; we'll include the event IDs.
[13:00] Karen (Ursa): The problem was we did notice higher tail latency during that window, users complained. Is there a way to guarantee p99 for certain routes?
[14:00] Diego (Redwood): For strict p99 SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity and pinned model version; we can offer a 99th percentile SLA as part of the Dedicated proposal.
[15:00] Emma (Redwood): Pricing tradeoffs — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency but has commit costs; hosted is flexible but can see variability under regional pressure.
[16:00] Samir (Ursa): Our decision criteria: predictable p99 < 300ms for core routes, cost under $X per 1M tokens, and SOC 2 + data residency. We need a pilot to validate.
[17:00] Karen (Ursa): Can you run a one-week benchmark on our staging dataset? We'll provision access.
[18:00] Diego (Redwood): Yes, we can run the benchmark — Diego: action: we'll run dedicated-staging benchmark with two configs (hosted optimized + dedicated small pool).
[19:00] Lina (Ursa): On networking, our security team requires SAML SSO and static egress IPs for webhooks — doable?
[20:00] Emma (Redwood): SAML SSO is supported; static egress IPs are available for Dedicated and Private. We'll document exact network requirements.
[21:00] Karen (Ursa): About cost optimization — any quick wins we can implement now?
[22:00] Diego (Redwood): Short term: enable prefix caching, tune batching thresholds, and set sampling for non-critical routes to a cheaper model. We'll send config snippets.
[23:00] Emma (Redwood): We'll include a recommended config diff and an estimated cost delta in the report.
[24:00] Samir (Ursa): Sounds good. If the Dedicated proposal lines up on price, we'll likely move forward with a pilot.
[25:00] Karen (Ursa): Timeline-wise we want Q4 validation. Target: pilot kickoff mid-Oct.
[26:00] Diego (Redwood): We'll aim to have a SOW and pilot runbook by 10/15.
[27:00] Emma (Redwood): Quick recap: Emma to send usage/cost report; Diego to prepare Dedicated proposal + SOW + config diffs + benchmarking plan; Karen to share staging access; Redwood to share SOC2 & KMS docs.
[28:00] Karen (Ursa): Anything else on roadmap alignment? We plan to expand to multi-region in Q1 and need guidance on routing policies.
[29:00] Diego (Redwood): We can support smart routing by policy (latency/region/cost). We'll include a recommended routing policy draft based on your multi-region plan.
[30:00] Samir (Ursa): Great. One last question — any hidden costs? e.g., request charges vs token charges?
[31:00] Emma (Redwood): No hidden fees; main levers are per-token compute, embeddings unit, and data transfer for Private. We'll detail this in the cost breakdown.
[32:00] Karen (Ursa): Ok thanks. We'll wait for the report.
[33:00] Diego (Redwood): Noted. We'll also include the exact incident timeline and event IDs for the Sept reliability blip.
[34:00] Emma (Redwood): Next steps and owners on the calendar; I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and share the resources.
[35:00] Lina (Ursa): Quick nit — can you include an estimate of per-request cost under the dedicated config?
[36:00] Diego (Redwood): Yes, estimate ranges will be in the proposal using your current traffic profile.
[37:00] Emma (Redwood): Any blockers from your side to start the pilot?
[38:00] Karen (Ursa): Just internal approvals — security wants the SOC docs before signing the SOW.
[39:00] Emma (Redwood): We'll send SOC 2 and network docs today. Expect an email from me after this call.
[40:00] Samir (Ursa): Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[41:00] Emma (Redwood): Thanks — we'll follow up on actions.
[42:00] (call ends)

Action Items (recap):
- Emma Chen: Send detailed usage + cost report for last 90 days (due 2025-10-10)
- Diego Rivera: Prepare Dedicated infra proposal, pilot SOW, and benchmarking plan (due 2025-10-15)
- Karen Holt: Share staging dataset access + expected SLAs (due 2025-10-12)

References/Artifacts: "QBR deck (shared)" link, "Usage export (will be shared)", "SOC2 report (will be shared)"
